source.title: Making LoRA Identifiable: Orthogonal Alignment for Continual Learning
source.authors: P. Singh; Mohammadi Zaki; Akash Saha; Aneesh Mukkamala; P. Wasnik

record.tranche_reason: Uses orthogonal Procrustes alignment of LoRA factors as part of a continual-learning method, but does not test whether models' representations of the same inputs become more similar with scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The study measures alignment-related quantities for LoRA factors learned across task updates, not distances between model representations of the same inputs. Its continual-learning accuracy and ablation results do not directly test the claim and are not included as rows. The reported factor-geometry findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study proposes a LoRA continual-learning method (SOAR). It aligns LoRA factor matrices of one model across sequential tasks with orthogonal Procrustes. It never compares representations of the same inputs across independently trained models, seeds, scales or modalities. It also does not rely on the convergence finding as a tool: its premise is LoRA factor asymmetry and non-identifiability, not cross-model convergence. It neither tests nor uses the claim. No relation enum fits exactly; 'discusses' is the nearest, since it only talks loosely about 'representational misalignment' of LoRA coordinates.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that Stiefel-constrained A and Procrustes-aligned, rank-wise gated merging of B reduce coordinate mismatch and forgetting. They report SOAR outperforming baselines at constant adapter memory. They note two limits: rank-wise retention may miss knowledge spread across subspaces, and fully overwritten information cannot be recovered without replay.
record.recipe_differences: The study's method aligns and merges sequentially updated LoRA factors for continual learning; it does not reproduce a method measuring convergence of model representations across scale, seeds, or modalities.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported LoRA-factor retention gate is higher for similar than dissimilar task transitions and varies by projection type. Principal-angle drift differs across task orders.

fits_no_version.finding: Within one model, the LoRA input-factor subspace drifts little across related tasks (3.50°, 5.04°) and more across diverse tasks (12.59°). The post-Procrustes gate is higher for similar tasks and varies by projection (Q≈0.94, K≈0.93, O≈0.81, V≈0.66).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometry of sequentially learned LoRA factors is more stable across related tasks and in query/key projections than in value projections.

record.problems: The alignment diagnostics concern LoRA factors, not distances between model representations of shared inputs. Figure 2 does not provide numerical values for the dissimilar-task gates in the text, and no uncertainty is reported for the alignment diagnostics.
record.rows_left_out: Continual-learning performance and ablation outcomes are not measurements of the claim's representation-convergence object, so they are not included as rows.

untested.parts: No cross-model representation similarity measured, and no scale or capability trend. The Table 3 size comparison is about task accuracy only.
No vision-language or paired cross-modal data.
Seeds 42–44 are used only for accuracy variance. Features or subspaces across seeds are not compared.
Procrustes maps LoRA B factors within one model across tasks. No mapping between different models' representations, and no stitching.
No interpretable features or circuits examined.
No similarity-metric or input dependence of representation convergence.
No assessment of how complete cross-model alignment is, or what causes it.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4/uses_without_test overstates the link. The paper does not cite or rely on the Platonic Representation Hypothesis or Convergent Learning. Its Procrustes step aligns LoRA parameter factors, not representations of shared inputs across models. It is outside the claim's scope: T6.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep measuring representation convergence.
No paired image-caption or other cross-modal alignment measurement.
No comparison of networks trained from different initializations for shared features or subspaces.
Procrustes maps are applied to LoRA factors from sequential task updates; the study does not test whether one model's input representations can be mapped to another's with little loss.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are examined.

Task relatedness and projection type vary in a LoRA-factor retention diagnostic, but the study does not test dependence of input-representation convergence on similarity metrics, their settings, or out-of-distribution inputs.
No test of whether shared training data or objectives explain convergence between models' input representations.
